question: What is Dark Matter?
short_answer: Dark matter is an invisible, non-luminous form of matter that makes up about 85% of all matter in the Universe, detected through its gravitational pull on stars and galaxies.
full_explanation: Vera Rubin proved dark matter exists by showing galactic rotation speeds remain flat at outer edges rather than slowing down, requiring an invisible mass halo.
